AIO is currently using a beta version of @angular/service-worker.
Since that was implemented, the SW has been rewritten and released
as part of Angular 5.0.0. This commit updates AIO to use the latest
implementation, with an appropriate configuration file that caches
the various AIO assets in useful ways.

issue.body:
[ ] It only do not update correctly, when client is login with gmail account, and do update.

## Current behavior
On release of new version of the app, update version pop is being displayed to the user, once they willingly press update, the version of app is not loading correctly. It throws some type error, saying cannot read id of undefined. It only happens, when client's browser is in user mode, not in guest mode. 
Guest mode goes fine, but it does not fulfill the purpose of using service worker. In guest mode, every time app is being loaded as its first access. Furthermore, when the app goes expire in browser, it only loads the service-worker.js, nothing else.

## Expected behavior
On release of new version of the app, update version pop is being displayed to the user, once they willingly press update, service worker should update the version correctly. 

## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions
https://staging.rxconcileapp.com
Install it in your latest chrome browser, with user mode. I deploy changes everyday on staging site. Reload after few days, you will see update popup in a minute or two. press update and check if you  guys could see the updated FE assets.


## Environment
Production

Angular version: Angular (all packages router, core, service worker, compiler-cli, forms, etc): 5.2.9

Browser:
- [ ] Chrome (desktop) Version 67.0.3386.1 (Official Build) dev (64-bit)

 
For Tooling issues:
-Typescript: 2.5.2,
-Angular-Cli: 1.7.4,
- Node version:8.9,4
- Platform:   CentOS, Windows

Let me know, if you guys need more info for debugging purpose.
Consider it an hotfix for me, App is in production, right now.

## PR Checklist
- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] ~~Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)~~


## PR Type
```
[x] Bugfix
```

## What is the current behavior?
Requests from clients that are not assigned a client ID by the browser will produce `fetch` events with `null` or empty (`''`) `clientId`s.

The ServiceWorker only handles `null` values correctly. Yet empty strings are also valid (see for example [here][1] and [there][2]).

Related Chromium issue/discussion: [#832105][3]

Issue Number: #23526

## What is the new behavior?
The SW will interpret _all_ falsy `clientId` valuesthe same (i.e. "no client ID assigned") and handle them appropriately.


## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?
```
[ ] Yes
[x] No
```


## Other information
Fixes #23526.

[1]: https://github.com/w3c/ServiceWorker/blob/4cc72bd0f13359f16cc733d88bed4ea52ee063c0/docs/index.bs#L1392
[2]: https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#fetchevent-interface
[3]: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=832105
